title: Canada's Charter lets Parliament or a legislature declare that an Act shall operate notwithstanding certain rights sections
summary: Canada's Charter lets Parliament or a legislature declare that an Act shall operate notwithstanding certain rights sections.
body: Section 33 says Parliament or the legislature of a province may expressly declare that an Act or a provision shall operate notwithstanding a provision included in section 2 or sections 7 to 15 of the Charter. The source says: "a provision thereof shall operate notwithstanding a provision included in section 2 or sections 7 to 15 of this Charter." The override is written into the Charter and is limited to the sections it names. It is not a power to set aside every part of the constitution. The consolidation also states how long a declaration operates.
